q: How many days of unemployment am I allowed on post-completion OPT?
expected: Up to 90 days of unemployment during post-completion OPT (150 total with the STEM extension).

q: Can I start working before my EAD start date?
expected: No. You may not begin OPT until the start date on your EAD.

q: When can I apply for post-completion OPT?
expected: Up to 90 days before your program end date and no later than 60 days after; within 30 days of the DSO's SEVIS recommendation.

q: Does part-time work count toward maintaining OPT status?
expected: Post-completion OPT must be at least 20 hours/week; below that you are considered unemployed.

q: How long is the grace period after my OPT ends?
expected: 60 days after the EAD expiration date.

q: How long is the STEM OPT extension, and who's eligible?
expected: 24 months, for students with a qualifying STEM degree, in valid post-completion OPT, with an E-Verify employer.

q: Do I need a job offer to apply for OPT?
expected: No job offer is required to apply for post-completion OPT.

q: How soon must I report a change of employer?
expected: Report changes (incl. employer) to your DSO within 10 days.

q: Can I travel internationally while on OPT?
expected: Generally yes with valid documents; specifics depend on EAD/job offer and cap-gap status. Confirm with DSO.

q: What is cap-gap?
expected: Automatic extension of F-1 status/OPT bridging the gap to an Oct 1 H-1B start for timely-filed cap-subject petitions.

q: Can I do volunteer or unpaid work to avoid unemployment days?
expected: Volunteer/unpaid work related to your field, at least 20 hrs/week and not violating labor laws, may count.

q: Is self-employment allowed on OPT?
expected: Self-employment can qualify on post-completion OPT if the business is related to the field and properly run; not allowed for STEM OPT.

q: What happens if my program ends while my OPT application is still pending?
expected: Post-completion OPT can be pending after program end; you may not work until the EAD is approved and its start date arrives.

q: Can I work for more than one employer on OPT?
expected: Yes on regular post-completion OPT (each job related to your field); STEM OPT requires bona fide employer-employee relationships and E-Verify.

q: Does my OPT job have to relate to my major?
expected: Yes. All OPT employment must be directly related to your major area of study.

q: What is the capital of France?
expected: OUT OF SCOPE - should refuse.

q: How many hours can I work on pre-completion OPT while school is in session?
expected: 20 hours or less per week while school is in session; full time when school is not in session.

q: Does time on pre-completion OPT reduce my post-completion OPT?
expected: Yes. Pre-completion OPT is deducted from post-completion OPT; a full year of full-time pre-completion OPT removes the post-completion year.

q: What happens if my STEM OPT extension is still pending when my current OPT expires?
expected: If the STEM extension was filed on time and OPT expires while it is pending, employment authorization is automatically extended for up to 180 days.

q: How long can my OPT request stay in Requested status before it is canceled?
expected: An OPT request left in Requested status longer than 180 days is automatically canceled by SEVIS.

q: What happens if I go over 90 days of unemployment on post-completion OPT?
expected: Exceeding 90 days of unemployment (150 with the STEM extension) can lead SEVP to terminate your SEVIS record.

q: How do I apply for the EAD, and which form do I file?
expected: File Form I-765 (Application for Employment Authorization) with USCIS, with the fee and required documentation, after your DSO recommends OPT in SEVIS.

q: Does my STEM OPT employer need to be enrolled in E-Verify?
expected: Yes. The STEM OPT extension requires employment with an employer enrolled in E-Verify.

q: How many months of OPT can I get for one degree level?
expected: Up to 12 months of OPT per education level; changing to a higher education level makes you eligible for another 12 months.

q: Must I report to my DSO if I have no employer or become unemployed?
expected: Yes. Report changes or interruptions in employment; a record with no current employer information counts as unemployment.

q: Do I pay Social Security and Medicare (FICA) taxes on my OPT income?
expected: Not covered by the official OPT sources - should refuse and defer to DSO/tax guidance.

q: Can I apply for a green card while I'm on OPT?
expected: Adjustment of status is out of scope for these sources - should refuse and defer to DSO/attorney.

q: What are my chances in the H-1B lottery?
expected: Not addressed in the OPT sources - should refuse.

q: What is the current USCIS processing time for my OPT application right now?
expected: Live processing times are not in the static sources - should refuse and point to USCIS/DSO.

q: Will my OPT application definitely be approved if I file everything on time?
expected: The sources do not guarantee approval - should refuse to promise an outcome and defer to DSO.
